extraction.name: ARC: The AI2 Reasoning Challenge
extraction.description: A dataset of 7,787 natural, grade-school science multiple-choice questions, partitioned into Challenge and Easy sets, released together with an ARC science corpus and baseline QA models to encourage advanced question answering and reasoning research.
extraction.creator: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord
extraction.citeAs: Clark, P., Cowhey, I., Etzioni, O., Khot, T., Sabharwal, A., Schoenick, C., & Tafjord, O. (2018). Think you have Solved Question Answering? Try ARC, the AI2 Reasoning Challenge.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The ARC dataset was assembled through several months of extensive search and investigation. Questions were drawn from a variety of standardized test sources, and the ARC Corpus was created by using a major search engine to run a large series of science-related search queries, collecting the top several documents from each search, de-duplicating them, stripping them down to text, and chunking the text into sentences.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Document analysis, Web Scraping, Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Natural science questions authored for standardized tests from multiple sources, plus science-related web documents retrieved via search queries for the ARC Corpus.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Several months of extensive search and investigation; no exact dates stated.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For the ARC Corpus, retrieved documents were de-duplicated, stripped down to text, and chunked into sentences. For questions, the dataset was partitioned into Challenge and Easy sets based on baseline solver performance.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were filtered to non-diagram multiple-choice science questions; Challenge questions were defined as those answered incorrectly by both retrieval-based and word co-occurrence solvers. For the ARC Corpus, long sentences, sentences with negation, and noisy sentences were filtered in the entailment pipeline.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The paper states that questions were authored for human tests and that target student grade levels were assigned by the examiners who authored the questions. For the Science Entailment dataset used to train entailment models, crowdworkers annotated premises and hypotheses as entailing or not.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Challenge questions were operationally defined by disagreement/failure of two baseline solvers (IR and PMI). The paper also notes that grade-level difficulty varies substantially within each grade and that the ARC Corpus was informally sampled for relevance.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Examiners who authored the questions assigned grade levels ranging from 3rd to 9th grade; no further annotator demographics are provided.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Elasticsearch was used for retrieval in the IR and entailment pipelines; Open IE and a chunker were used for DGEM structured representations; the paper also mentions a proprietary parser in DGEM.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The ARC Dataset, Corpus, baseline models, and leaderboard are publicly available at the ARC website; the paper does not specify versioning, update schedule, maintainers, or deprecation policy.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Grade level / age range of intended students (3rd to 9th grade, approximately ages 8 through 13).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to advance AI research in advanced question answering and reasoning beyond surface-level cues, with the broader goal of improving community progress on harder QA tasks.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that many QA datasets are biased toward surface-level cues and simple algorithms; ARC was designed to reduce this by filtering out questions answered by retrieval and co-occurrence methods. It also notes that grade levels overlap substantially in difficulty.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The Challenge Set is difficult for simple retrieval and co-occurrence methods, and even baseline neural models do not significantly outperform random guessing on it. The corpus does not guarantee that a single sentence explicitly answers a question, and some knowledge is only indirectly represented. Use of the ARC Corpus is optional and systems are not restricted to it.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing for multiple-choice question answering and reasoning research; the paper also presents the dataset as a community challenge and benchmark.
